claim: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) have long been shown to exist as oligomers with functional properties distinct from those of the monomeric counterparts.
source: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) have long been shown to exist as oligomers with functional properties distinct from those of the monomeric counterparts, but the driving factors of oligomerization remain relatively unexplored.
evidence: This is a general statement about GPCRs supported by the broader scientific literature, as indicated by the context of the introduction.

claim: The intrinsically disordered C-terminus of A2AR drives receptor homo-oligomerization.
source: Combining experimental and computational approaches, we discover that the intrinsically disordered C-terminus of A2AR drives receptor homo-oligomerization.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental SEC data showing progressive decline in oligomerization with C-terminus truncation (Figure 3B) and MD simulations showing C-terminus involvement in dimeric interfaces (Figure 4A).

claim: The formation of A2AR oligomers declines progressively with the shortening of the C-terminus.
source: The formation of A2AR oligomers declines progressively with the shortening of the C-terminus.
evidence: This is directly supported by SEC experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Multiple interaction types are responsible for A2AR oligomerization, including disulfide linkages, hydrogen bonds, electrostatic interactions, and hydrophobic interactions.
source: Multiple interaction types are responsible for A2AR oligomerization, including disulfide linkages, hydrogen bonds, electrostatic interactions, and hydrophobic interactions.
evidence: This is supported by TCEP reduction experiments (Figure 2B), MD simulations showing electrostatic contacts and hydrogen bonds (Figure 4B, C), and DSF experiments showing hydrophobic interactions (Figure 6B).

claim: These interactions are enhanced by depletion interactions, giving rise to a tunable network of bonds that allow A2AR oligomers to adopt multiple interfaces.
source: These interactions are enhanced by depletion interactions, giving rise to a tunable network of bonds that allow A2AR oligomers to adopt multiple interfaces.
evidence: This is supported by ionic strength experiments showing increased oligomerization at higher ionic strengths (Figure 5).

claim: GPCR oligomers can have properties distinct from monomeric protomers in ligand binding.
source: The properties emerging from these oligomers can be distinct from those of the monomeric protomers in ligand binding (El-Asmar et al., 2005; Casadó-Anguera et al., 2016; Guitart et al., 2014; Yoshioka et al., 2001)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: GPCR oligomers can have properties distinct from monomeric protomers in G protein coupling.
source: The properties emerging from these oligomers can be distinct from those of the monomeric protomers in ligand binding (El-Asmar et al., 2005; Casadó-Anguera et al., 2016; Guitart et al., 2014; Yoshioka et al., 2001), G protein coupling (Cristóvão-Ferreira et al., 2013; Cordomí et al., 2015; González-Maeso et al., 2007; Lee et al., 2004; Rashid et al., 2007)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: GPCR oligomers can have properties distinct from monomeric protomers in downstream signaling.
source: The properties emerging from these oligomers can be distinct from those of the monomeric protomers in ligand binding (El-Asmar et al., 2005; Casadó-Anguera et al., 2016; Guitart et al., 2014; Yoshioka et al., 2001), G protein coupling (Cristóvão-Ferreira et al., 2013; Cordomí et al., 2015; González-Maeso et al., 2007; Lee et al., 2004; Rashid et al., 2007), downstream signaling (Liu et al., 2016; Hilairet et al., 2003; Rozenfeld and Devi, 2007; Borroto-Escuela et al., 2010)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: GPCR oligomers can have properties distinct from monomeric protomers in receptor internalization/desensitization.
source: The properties emerging from these oligomers can be distinct from those of the monomeric protomers in ligand binding (El-Asmar et al., 2005; Casadó-Anguera et al., 2016; Guitart et al., 2014; Yoshioka et al., 2001), G protein coupling (Cristóvão-Ferreira et al., 2013; Cordomí et al., 2015; González-Maeso et al., 2007; Lee et al., 2004; Rashid et al., 2007), downstream signaling (Liu et al., 2016; Hilairet et al., 2003; Rozenfeld and Devi, 2007; Borroto-Escuela et al., 2010), and receptor internalization/desensitization (Ecke et al., 2008; Stanasila et al., 2003; Faklaris et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: GPCR oligomers with multiple interfaces can give rise to myriad ways by which these complexes can be formed and their functions modulated.
source: GPCR oligomers with multiple interfaces (Song et al., 2020; Ghosh et al., 2014; Periole et al., 2012; Fanelli and Felline, 2011; Liu et al., 2012) can give rise to myriad ways by which these complexes can be formed and their functions modulated.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: In the crystal structure of the turkey β1-adrenergic receptor (β1AR), the receptor appears to dimerize via two different interfaces, one formed via TM4/TM5 and the other via TM1/TM2/H8 contacts.
source: In the crystal structure of the turkey β1-adrenergic receptor (β1AR), the receptor appears to dimerize via two different interfaces, one formed via TM4/TM5 (transmembrane domains 4/5) and the other via TM1/TM2/H8 (helix 8) contacts (Huang et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a published crystal structure study.

claim: In the crystal structure of the antagonist-bound μ-opioid receptor (μ-OR), the protomers dimerize via two interfaces, but only one of them is predicted to induce a steric hindrance that prevents activation of both protomers.
source: Similarly, in the crystal structure of the antagonist-bound μ-opioid receptor (μ-OR), the protomers also dimerize via two interfaces; however, only one of them is predicted to induce a steric hindrance that prevents activation of both protomers (Manglik et al., 2012), hinting at interface-specific functional consequences.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a published crystal structure study.

claim: A computational study predicted that the adenosine A2A receptor (A2AR) forms homodimers via three different interfaces and that the resulting dimeric architectures can modulate receptor function in different or even opposite ways.
source: A recent computational study predicted that the adenosine A2A receptor (A2AR) forms homodimers via three different interfaces and that the resulting dimeric architectures can modulate receptor function in different or even opposite ways (Fanelli and Felline, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a published computational study.

claim: Asymmetric interfaces have been reported in M3 muscarinic receptor, rhodopsin, and opsin.
source: Asymmetric interfaces, reported in M3 muscarinic receptor (Thorsen et al., 2014), rhodopsin (Fotiadis et al., 2006; Fotiadis et al., 2003; Liang et al., 2003), and opsin (Liang et al., 2003), are in contrast formed with the protomers positioning face-to-back, possibly enabling the association of higher-order oligomers.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: A2AR oligomers can adopt eight different interfaces that interconvert when the receptor is activated or when there are changes in the local membrane environment.
source: According to a recent computational study, A2AR oligomers can adopt eight different interfaces that interconvert when the receptor is activated or when there are changes in the local membrane environment (Song et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a published computational study.

claim: Neurotensin receptor 1 (NTS1R) dimer is formed by 'rolling' interfaces that coexist and interconvert when the receptor is activated.
source: Similarly, a recent study that combined experimental and computational data proposed that neurotensin receptor 1 (NTS1R) dimer is formed by 'rolling' interfaces that coexist and interconvert when the receptor is activated (Dijkman et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: The cytosolic carboxy (C-)terminus of GPCRs is usually an IDR.
source: The cytosolic carboxy (C-)terminus of GPCRs is usually an IDR (Tovo-Rodrigues et al., 2014; Jaakola et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The C-terminus of GPCRs is commonly removed in structural studies to enhance receptor stability and conformational homogeneity.
source: Varying in length among different GPCRs, the C-terminus is commonly removed in structural studies of GPCRs to enhance receptor stability and conformational homogeneity.
evidence: This is a general statement about structural biology practices supported by established knowledge in the field.

claim: A2AR has a 122-residue C-terminus that is truncated in all published structural biology studies.
source: A striking example is A2AR, a model GPCR with a particularly long, 122-residue, C-terminus that is truncated in all published structural biology studies (Song et al., 2020; Fanelli and Felline, 2011; García-Nafría et al., 2018; Sun et al., 2017; Lebon et al., 2011; Xu et al., 2011; Doré et al., 2011; Jaakola et al., 2008; Carpenter et al., 2016; Hino et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple published structural studies.

claim: C-terminal truncations of GPCRs have been shown to affect GPCR downstream signaling.
source: However, evidence is accumulating that such truncations—shown to affect GPCR downstream signaling (Koretz et al., 2021; Navarro et al., 2018a; Jain and McGraw, 2020)—may abolish receptor oligomerization (Schonenbach et al., 2016; Svetlana and Devi, 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: C-terminal truncations may abolish receptor oligomerization.
source: However, evidence is accumulating that such truncations—shown to affect GPCR downstream signaling (Koretz et al., 2021; Navarro et al., 2018a; Jain and McGraw, 2020)—may abolish receptor oligomerization (Schonenbach et al., 2016; Svetlana and Devi, 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: C-terminally truncated A2AR does not show protein aggregation or clustering on the cell surface, a process readily observed in the wild-type form.
source: A study using immunofluorescence has demonstrated that C-terminally truncated A2AR does not show protein aggregation or clustering on the cell surface, a process readily observed in the wild-type form (Burgueño et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a published immunofluorescence study.

claim: A single-residue substitution of a C-terminal cysteine, C394S, reduces A2AR homo-oligomerization in vitro.
source: Our recent study employing a tandem three-step chromatography approach uncovered the impact of a single-residue substitution of a C-terminal cysteine, C394S, in reducing the receptor homo-oligomerization in vitro (Schonenbach et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study by the authors.

claim: A2AR-D2R dimerization occurs via direct electrostatic interactions between the C-terminus of A2AR and the third intracellular loop of D2R.
source: In the context of heteromerization, mass spectrometry and pull-down experiments have demonstrated that A2AR-D2R dimerization occurs via direct electrostatic interactions between the C-terminus of A2AR and the third intracellular loop of D2R (Ciruela et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a published mass spectrometry and pull-down study.

claim: SEC analysis separated A2AR into distinct oligomeric species: high-molecular-weight (HMW) oligomer, dimer, and monomer.
source: Distinct oligomeric species were separated and eluted in the following order: high-molecular-weight (HMW) oligomer, dimer, and monomer (Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is directly supported by SEC chromatogram data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The peak assignment of A2AR oligomeric species has been verified with SEC-MALS experiments.
source: This peak assignment has been verified with SEC-MALS (multi-angle light scattering) experiments, as detailed in a previous publication (Schonenbach et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous publication.

claim: The dimer level of A2AR-WT was significantly higher than that of the A2AR-C394X variants.
source: We found that the dimer level of A2AR-WT was significantly higher than that of the A2AR-C394X variants (WT: 1.14; C394X: 0.24–0.57; Figure 2A).
evidence: This is directly supported by SEC experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Residue C394 plays a role in A2AR oligomerization, and even more prominently in A2AR dimerization.
source: This suggests that residue C394 plays a role in A2AR oligomerization, and even more prominently in A2AR dimerization.
evidence: This is inferred from the SEC data showing reduced oligomerization in C394X variants (Figure 2A).

claim: Upon incubation with TCEP, the dimer level of the A2AR-WT sample decreased from 1.14 to 0.51.
source: Upon incubation with TCEP, the dimer level of the A2AR-WT sample decreased from 1.14 to 0.51 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is directly supported by western blot densitometry data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Disulfide bond formation via residue C394 is one possible mechanism for A2AR dimerization.
source: This indicates that disulfide bond formation via residue C394 is one possible mechanism for A2AR dimerization.
evidence: This is inferred from the TCEP reduction experiment showing decreased dimer levels (Figure 2B).

claim: The dimer level of the A2AR-Q372ΔC sample decreased from 0.68 to 0.22 upon incubation with TCEP.
source: Interestingly, the dimer level of the A2AR-Q372ΔC sample also decreased from 0.68 to 0.22 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is directly supported by western blot densitometry data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: There may exist other inter-A2AR disulfide bonds that do not involve residue C394.
source: This suggests that there may exist other inter-A2AR disulfide bonds that do not involve residue C394.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Q372ΔC (lacking C394) still shows TCEP-sensitive dimers.

claim: A clearly visible population of A2AR dimer persists even after reduction of disulfide bonds via TCEP.
source: Still, in both cases, a clearly visible population of A2AR dimer persists, even after reduction of disulfide bonds via TCEP (Figure 2B), suggesting that there must be additional interfacial sites that help drive A2AR dimer/oligomerization.
evidence: This is directly supported by western blot data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: There must be additional interfacial sites that help drive A2AR dimer/oligomerization beyond disulfide bonds.
source: Still, in both cases, a clearly visible population of A2AR dimer persists, even after reduction of disulfide bonds via TCEP (Figure 2B), suggesting that there must be additional interfacial sites that help drive A2AR dimer/oligomerization.
evidence: This is inferred from the persistence of dimers after TCEP treatment.

claim: Both the dimer and the total oligomer levels of A2AR decreased progressively with the shortening of the C-terminus.
source: Both the dimer and the total oligomer levels of A2AR decreased progressively with the shortening of the C-terminus, with almost no oligomerization detected upon complete truncation of the C-terminus at site A316 (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is directly supported by SEC experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Almost no oligomerization was detected upon complete truncation of the C-terminus at site A316.
source: Both the dimer and the total oligomer levels of A2AR decreased progressively with the shortening of the C-terminus, with almost no oligomerization detected upon complete truncation of the C-terminus at site A316 (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is directly supported by SEC experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The C-terminus drives A2AR oligomerization, with multiple potential interaction sites positioned along much of its length.
source: This result shows that the C-terminus drives A2AR oligomerization, with multiple potential interaction sites positioned along much of its length.
evidence: This is inferred from the progressive decrease in oligomerization with systematic C-terminus truncation.

claim: There occurred a dramatic decrease in the dimer level between the N359 and P354 truncation sites, from a value of 0.81 to 0.19.
source: Interestingly, there occurred a dramatic decrease in the dimer level between the N359 and P354 truncation sites, from a value of 0.81 to 0.19, respectively (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is directly supported by SEC experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The C-terminal segment encompassing residues 354–359 is a key constituent of the A2AR oligomeric interface.
source: Clearly, the C-terminal segment encompassing residues 354–359 (highlighted in black in Figure 3A) is a key constituent of the A2AR oligomeric interface.
evidence: This is inferred from the dramatic decrease in oligomerization when this segment is removed.

claim: The ERR:AAA mutations had varied effects on the dimer level: decreasing for A2AR-FL-WT but increasing for A2AR-N359ΔC.
source: We found that the ERR:AAA mutations had varied effects on the dimer level: decreasing for A2AR-FL-WT (ctrl: 0.49; ERR:AAA: 0.29) but increasing for A2AR-N359ΔC (ctrl: 0.33; ERR:AAA: 0.48) (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is directly supported by SEC experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The ERR:AAA mutations reduced the HMW oligomer level of both A2AR-FL-WT and A2AR-N359ΔC.
source: In contrast, the ERR:AAA mutations reduced the HMW oligomer level of both A2AR-FL-WT (ctrl: 0.88; ERR:AAA: 0.66) and A2AR-N359ΔC (ctrl: 0.68; ERR:AAA: 0.38) (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is directly supported by SEC experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The charged residues 355ERR357 participate in A2AR oligomerization, with a greater effect in the context of a longer C-terminus and for forming higher-order oligomers.
source: These results suggest that the charged residues 355ERR357 participate in A2AR oligomerization, with a greater effect in the context of a longer C-terminus and for forming higher-order oligomers.
evidence: This is inferred from the ERR:AAA mutation experiments showing differential effects on oligomerization.

claim: A2AR dimers were formed with multiple interfaces, all involving the C-terminus only.
source: Our results revealed that A2AR dimers were formed with multiple interfaces, all involving the C-terminus only (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is directly supported by CGMD simulation data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The transmembrane heptahelical bundles were not a part of the dimeric interfaces as they all showed distances greater than the minimum distance criterion of 7 Å for interacting helices.
source: The transmembrane heptahelical bundles were not a part of the dimeric interfaces as they all showed distances greater than the minimum distance criterion of 7 Å for interacting helices.
evidence: This is directly supported by CGMD simulation analysis.

claim: The vast majority of A2AR dimers were symmetric, with the C-termini of the protomers directly interacting with each other.
source: The vast majority of A2AR dimers were symmetric, with the C-termini of the protomers directly interacting with each other.
evidence: This is directly supported by CGMD simulation analysis.

claim: A smaller fraction of the dimers had asymmetric orientations, with the C-terminus of one protomer interacting with other parts of the other protomer, such as ICL2 and ICL3.
source: A smaller fraction of the dimers had asymmetric orientations, with the C-terminus of one protomer interacting with other parts of the other protomer, such as ICL2 (the second intracellular loop) and ICL3 (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is directly supported by CGMD simulation data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: With the least truncated A2AR variant containing the longest C-terminus, A2AR-C394ΔC, an average of 15.9 electrostatic contacts were observed between the C-termini of the protomers.
source: With the least truncated A2AR variant containing the longest C-terminus, A2AR-C394ΔC, we observed an average of 15.9 electrostatic contacts (Figure 4B) and 26.7 hydrogen bonds (Figure 4C) between the C-termini of the protomers.
evidence: This is directly supported by CGMD simulation analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: With the least truncated A2AR variant containing the longest C-terminus, A2AR-C394ΔC, an average of 26.7 hydrogen bonds were observed between the C-termini of the protomers.
source: With the least truncated A2AR variant containing the longest C-terminus, A2AR-C394ΔC, we observed an average of 15.9 electrostatic contacts (Figure 4B) and 26.7 hydrogen bonds (Figure 4C) between the C-termini of the protomers.
evidence: This is directly supported by atomistic MD simulation analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Both electrostatic interactions and hydrogen bonds can play important roles in A2AR dimer formation.
source: This result shows that both electrostatic interactions and hydrogen bonds can play important roles in A2AR dimer formation.
evidence: This is inferred from the MD simulation data showing numerous electrostatic contacts and hydrogen bonds.

claim: Upon further C-terminus truncation, the average number of both electrostatic contacts and hydrogen bonds involving C-terminal residues progressively declined.
source: Upon further C-terminus truncation, the average number of both electrostatic contacts and hydrogen bonds involving C-terminal residues progressively declined, respectively reaching 5.4 and 6.0 for A2AR-A316ΔC (in which the disordered region of the C-terminus is removed) (Figure 4B, C).
evidence: This is directly supported by MD simulation analysis shown in Figure 4B and 4C.

claim: Truncation of a C-terminal segment reduces inter-A2AR contacts elsewhere along the C-terminus, indicating that an allosteric mechanism of dimerization exists.
source: This observation that truncation of a C-terminal segment reduces inter-A2AR contacts elsewhere along the C-terminus indicates that an allosteric mechanism of dimerization exists, in which an extended C-terminus of A2AR stabilizes inter-A2AR interactions near the heptahelical bundles of the dimeric complex.
evidence: This is inferred from the MD simulation data showing reduced contacts in segment 291-334 upon truncation of segment 335-394.

claim: At the low ionic strength of 0.15 M, the dimer and total oligomer levels of all four A2AR variants were near zero.
source: We found that the dimer and total oligomer levels of all four variants were near zero (Figure 5).
evidence: This is directly supported by SEC experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Electrostatic and hydrogen-bonding interactions are not the dominant driving force for A2AR association.
source: This is a striking experimental observation: despite being shown to play a role in stabilizing A2AR dimers according to our MD simulations (Figure 4B, C), we can conclude that electrostatic and hydrogen-bonding interactions are not the dominant driving force for A2AR association.
evidence: This is inferred from the near-zero oligomerization at low ionic strength where these interactions should be intact.

claim: At higher ionic strengths of 0.45 M and 0.95 M, the dimer and total oligomer levels of A2AR-V334ΔC remained near zero.
source: At higher ionic strengths of 0.45 M and 0.95 M, the dimer and total oligomer levels of A2AR-V334ΔC still remained near zero (Figure 5).
evidence: This is directly supported by SEC experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: A progressive and significant increase in the dimer and total oligomer levels of A2AR-FL-WT was observed with increasing ionic strength.
source: In contrast, we observed a progressive and significant increase in the dimer and total oligomer levels of A2AR-FL-WT with increasing ionic strength (Figure 5).
evidence: This is directly supported by SEC experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: A2AR oligomerization is driven by depletion interactions enhanced with increasing ionic strength and these interactions must involve the C-terminal segment after residue V334.
source: This result indicates that A2AR oligomerization is driven by depletion interactions enhanced with increasing ionic strength and that these interactions must involve the C-terminal segment after residue V334.
evidence: This is inferred from the ionic strength experiments showing increased oligomerization for FL-WT but not V334ΔC.

claim: The charged cluster 355ERR357 and the C-terminal segment after residue N359 promote the depletion interactions to drive A2AR oligomerization.
source: These results indicate that the charged cluster 355ERR357 and the C-terminal segment after residue N359 promote the depletion interactions to drive A2AR oligomerization.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential effects of ionic strength on FL-WT, FL-ERR:AAA, and N359ΔC variants.

claim: A2AR oligomerization is more robust when the C-terminus is fully present and the ionic strength higher.
source: Taken together, we can conclude that A2AR oligomerization is more robust when the C-terminus is fully present and the ionic strength higher, suggesting that depletion interactions via the C-terminus are strong driving factors of A2AR oligomerization.
evidence: This is inferred from the ionic strength experiments.

claim: The SEC-separated monomers repopulate into dimer/oligomer, with the total oligomer level after redistribution comparable with that of the initial samples for both A2AR-WT and Q372ΔC.
source: We found that the SEC-separated monomers repopulate into dimer/oligomer, with the total oligomer level after redistribution comparable with that of the initial samples for both A2AR-WT (initial: 2.87; redistributed: 1.60) and Q372ΔC (initial: 1.49; redistributed: 1.40) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is directly supported by SEC experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: A2AR oligomer is a thermodynamic product with a lower free energy compared with that of the monomer.
source: This observation indicates that A2AR oligomer is a thermodynamic product with a lower free energy compared with that of the monomer (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is inferred from the repopulation of monomers into oligomers.

claim: The SEC-separated dimer/oligomer populations do not repopulate to form monomers.
source: In contrast, the SEC-separated dimer/oligomer populations do not repopulate to form monomers (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is directly supported by SEC experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Once the oligomers are formed, some are kinetically trapped and thus cannot redistribute into monomers.
source: This observation is consistent with a published study of ours on A2AR dimers (Schonenbach et al., 2016), indicating that once the oligomers are formed, some are kinetically trapped and thus cannot redistribute into monomers.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of repopulation of oligomers into monomers and supported by citation.

claim: Disulfide linkages are likely candidates to kinetically stabilize A2AR oligomers.
source: We believe that disulfide linkages are likely candidates to kinetically stabilize A2AR oligomers, as demonstrated by their redistribution into monomers only in the presence of a reducing agent (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is inferred from the TCEP reduction experiments and the kinetic trapping observations.

claim: At NaCl concentrations below 1 M, the A2AR C-terminal peptide was dominantly soluble, despite showing slight aggregation at NaCl concentrations between 250 and 500 mM.
source: At NaCl concentrations below 1 M, the peptide was dominantly soluble, despite showing slight aggregation at NaCl concentrations between 250 and 500 mM (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is directly supported by UV-Vis absorption data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: At NaCl concentrations above 1 M, A2AR C-terminal peptides strongly associated into insoluble aggregates.
source: At NaCl concentrations above 1 M, A2AR C-terminal peptides strongly associated into insoluble aggregates (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is directly supported by UV-Vis absorption data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The A2AR C-terminus showed the tendency to progressively associate and eventually precipitate with increasing ionic strengths, suggesting that depletion interactions drive the association and precipitation of the peptides.
source: Consistent with the observations made with the intact receptor (Figure 5), the A2AR C-terminus showed the tendency to progressively associate and eventually precipitate with increasing ionic strengths, suggesting that depletion interactions drive the association and precipitation of the peptides.
evidence: This is inferred from the aggregation assay data showing increased aggregation with NaCl.

claim: The A2AR C-terminus incubated in 4 M GdnHCl showed no aggregation propensity.
source: Our results demonstrated that the A2AR C-terminus incubated in 4 M GdnHCl showed no aggregation propensity (Figure 6A), validating our expectation that salting-in salts do not enhance depletion interactions.
evidence: This is directly supported by UV-Vis absorption data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The C-terminal peptide in and of itself, outside the context of the lipid membrane and TM domain, can directly interact with other C-terminal peptides to form self-aggregates in the presence of ions that have salting-out effects.
source: These observations demonstrate that the C-terminal peptide in and of itself, outside the context of the lipid membrane and TM domain, can directly interact with other C-terminal peptides to form self-aggregates in the presence of ions, and presumably solutes, that have salting-out effects.
evidence: This is inferred from the aggregation assay data.

claim: As the temperature increased, a steady rise in fluorescence was observed in DSF experiments with the A2AR C-terminus.
source: Our results showed that as the temperature increased, a steady rise in fluorescence was observed (Figure 6B), indicating that multiple hydrophobic residues were gradually exposed to the SYPRO dye.
evidence: This is directly supported by DSF data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: At approximately 65°C, the melt peak signal was abruptly quenched in DSF experiments with the A2AR C-terminus.
source: However, at approximately 65°C, the melt peak signal was abruptly quenched (Figure 6B), indicating that the hydrophobic residues were no longer exposed to the dye.
evidence: This is directly supported by DSF data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: At 65°C, enough hydrophobic residues in the C-terminal peptides become exposed such that they collapse on one another, resulting in aggregation.
source: This observation suggests that, at 65°C, enough hydrophobic residues in the C-terminal peptides become exposed such that they collapse on one another (thus expelling the bound dye molecules), resulting in aggregation.
evidence: This is inferred from the DSF data showing fluorescence quenching.

claim: An average of 60 non-polar contacts were observed for A2AR-C394ΔC symmetrical dimers.
source: Specifically, we observed an average of 60 non-polar contacts for A2AR-C394ΔC.
evidence: This is directly supported by CGMD simulation analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The number of non-polar contacts progressively declined upon further C-terminus truncation, reaching 15 for A2AR-A316ΔC.
source: This number progressively declined upon further C-terminus truncation, reaching 15 for A2AR-A316ΔC.
evidence: This is directly supported by CGMD simulation analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The hydrophobic effect can cause A2AR C-terminal peptides to directly associate.
source: Clearly, the hydrophobic effect can cause A2AR C-terminal peptides to directly associate.
evidence: This is inferred from the DSF and MD simulation data showing hydrophobic interactions.

claim: A2AR oligomer formation can be driven by depletion interactions among the C-termini of the protomers by non-polar contacts.
source: These results demonstrate that A2AR oligomer formation can be driven by depletion interactions among the C-termini of the protomers by non-polar contacts.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined DSF, aggregation assay, and MD simulation data.

claim: The C-terminus of A2AR, removed in all previously published structural studies, is directly responsible for receptor oligomerization.
source: The key finding of this study is that the C-terminus of A2AR, removed in all previously published structural studies, is directly responsible for receptor oligomerization.
evidence: This is the main conclusion supported by all experimental and computational data in the study.

claim: The C-terminus stabilizes A2AR oligomers via a combination of disulfide linkages, hydrogen bonds, electrostatic interactions, and hydrophobic interactions.
source: Using a combination of experimental and computational approaches, we demonstrate that the C-terminus stabilizes A2AR oligomers via a combination of disulfide linkages, hydrogen bonds, electrostatic interactions, and hydrophobic interactions.
evidence: This is supported by multiple experimental and computational results throughout the study.

claim: This diverse combination of interactions is greatly enhanced by depletion interactions, forming a network of malleable bonds that drives A2AR oligomerization and gives rise to multiple oligomeric interfaces.
source: This diverse combination of interactions is greatly enhanced by depletion interactions, forming a network of malleable bonds that drives A2AR oligomerization and gives rise to multiple oligomeric interfaces.
evidence: This is supported by ionic strength experiments and MD simulations showing multiple interfaces.

claim: Residue C394 is highly conserved and a C-terminal cysteine is almost always present in A2AR homologs.
source: Indeed, this cysteine is highly conserved and a C-terminal cysteine is almost always present in A2AR homologs (Pándy-Szekeres et al., 2018), suggesting that it may serve an important role in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by citation to a database or comparative study.

claim: C-terminus truncation resulted in structural changes in the heptahelical bundles of A2AR dimers.
